headline: Tech and Energy Lead a Broad Thursday Rally as Healthcare Lags
body_html:
Thursday's session closed on a constructive note, with 360 stocks advancing against 180 declining across our 544-name universe. Semiconductors topped the sector table, rising 1.68%, while Software followed closely at 1.66%, and Energy contributed a solid 1.40% gain — a combination that gave the day a distinctly cyclical, risk-on character. Industrials added 1.18%, rounding out what amounted to a well-distributed advance through the market's growth and economically sensitive corners.

The day's unmistakable standout was Synopsys, which surged 12.78% to lead all gainers. The electronic design automation specialist was joined by Fair Isaac, up 11.69%, and optical-networking names Coherent and Ciena, which climbed 10.90% and 7.77% respectively — a cluster of moves that amplified the semiconductor and software gains. Credo Technology and Ubiquiti each rose more than 7%, keeping the networking complex firmly in focus.

Healthcare was the sole sector in the red, falling 1.35%, dragged lower by declines in life-sciences tools and biotech. Corteva's historic 83.81% collapse stood apart from every other move on the tape and merits close scrutiny in the sessions ahead. With Friday's monthly jobs report on the calendar, Thursday's broad advance may soon face a significant macro test.

briefs.headline: Synopsys Surges to Head of the Class in Thursday's Rally
briefs.body: Synopsys posted a 12.78% gain on Thursday, the largest advance in our universe for the session. The electronic design automation firm's move amplified a broader run in software and semiconductor names, underscoring continued investor appetite for infrastructure plays tied to chip design.

briefs.headline: Corteva Collapses 83.81% in a Session-Defining Decline
briefs.body: Agricultural-sciences company Corteva shed 83.81% on Thursday in a move that dwarfed every other loss on the tape. The severity of the drop suggests a company-specific event of significant magnitude, and traders will be watching closely for any clarifying disclosures in the hours ahead.

briefs.headline: Boeing Engineers Ratify New Contract, Averting a Work Stoppage
briefs.body: Boeing's engineers and technical workforce voted to approve a new labor agreement on Thursday, removing the immediate threat of a strike at the aerospace giant. The resolution eases a key operational risk for the manufacturer at a time when it has been working to stabilize production schedules and rebuild customer confidence.

briefs.headline: Jobs Report Looms as Friday's Pivotal Macro Catalyst
briefs.body: The September employment report is due Friday morning, and its reading on payrolls, wages, and unemployment could quickly reset expectations for Federal Reserve policy heading into year-end. Thursday's constructive session leaves equity markets in a relatively strong posture heading into the data release.

briefs.headline: US Sanctions Tighten on Iran's Transport Sectors
briefs.body: Washington announced new sanctions targeting Iran's automotive and rail industries following a shipping-lane blockade, adding fresh pressure to an already strained economic relationship. The move drew muted but attentive reaction in energy markets, where geopolitical risk premiums have remained a consistent undercurrent this autumn.

briefs.headline: Optical-Networking Names Ride the Session's Momentum
briefs.body: Coherent and Ciena advanced 10.90% and 7.77% respectively on Thursday, pushing the networking-optical subsector into the spotlight alongside semiconductors. The twin gains suggest investors are rotating into hardware that underpins high-capacity data infrastructure, a theme that has gathered pace through the third quarter.
